meta.session_title: Day 1 - Introduction to Java & Language Fundamentals
meta.instructions: Match each Java concept on the LEFT with its correct definition or example on the RIGHT. Drag and drop to pair them.

match.content: Java Development Kit = JRE + development tools (javac, javadoc, jar). Required to write and compile Java programs.
Correct data type for 18-digit bank account numbers. Uses 'L' suffix to indicate a long literal (otherwise compiler treats it as int).
Prints: 5  (post-increment: use current value 5, THEN increment x to 6)
Thrown when accessing arr[i] where i < 0 or i >= arr.length. Common bug: using i <= arr.length instead of i < arr.length in a loop.
Write Once, Run Anywhere — Java compiles to bytecode (.class) that any JVM can run, regardless of OS (Windows, Linux, macOS).
Safe null-tolerant String comparison. Returns false if bankCode is null (no NullPointerException). Always prefer literal.equals(variable).
Java constant declaration: 'final' prevents reassignment. UPPER_SNAKE_CASE naming convention. 'static' means it belongs to the class, not an instance.
In (A && B): if A is false, B is skipped. Used for safety: (account != null && account.isActive()) — avoids NullPointerException if account is null.
Prints: false — floating-point precision error: 0.1+0.2 = 0.30000000000000004. Use BigDecimal for monetary calculations in banking systems.
When a switch case matches, execution continues into ALL subsequent cases until a 'break' or end of switch. Missing 'break' is a common bug in transaction-type routing.
